title: Stitch: Micro-Remediator Tasklet Framework and Contextual Admin Fuse
creator: Maya R. Chen
description: Build a small-footprint framework ("Stitch") that lets oncall and support engineers author, validate, and execute micro-remediation tasklets that are automatically contextualized with runtime metadata. The goal is to reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) for common operator flows by providing reusable, auditable, and safely gated primitives that can be invoked from the Console, CLI, or incident robot. Tasklets should be composable, idempotent, and include prechecks, dry-run, and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: SDK + YAML schema for tasklet metadata and typed inputs
Tasklet runtime can run isolated with RBAC enforcement and logging to ops-telemetry
Precheck / dry-run returns deterministic simulated outcome for 80% of core tasklets
Console integration: execute a tasklet from the support run panel with confirmation modal
Audit trail: every execution produces a trace link, execution payload, and exit code stored for 90 days
Safety: bounded rate and scope (namespace-limited) and automatic abort on 3 failed attempts
design_notes: Prefer a minimal sandboxed execution harness vs. full container for speed. Initial PoC uses short-lived language trap process (Go sandbox) to avoid heavy infra changes.
Tasklet authoring is YAML-first with optional TypeScript/Go helpers for advanced logic.
We will reuse existing RBAC service for permission checks and reuse the runbook telemetry schema for eventing to avoid new storage schemas.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive tasklet published with wide scope. Mitigation: require two-step approval for publish and a canary namespace flag.
Risk: long-running tasklets blocking agents. Mitigation: enforce hard wall timeouts and watchdog restarts.
Risk: audit logs leak secrets. Mitigation: automatic redaction of matching KMS keys/hints before persisting payloads.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Schema & PoC runtime (local harness) + YAML authoring CLI
Week 2: Console invoke button + confirmation modal + telemetry hook
Week 3: RBAC gating, approval flow integration, and publishing UI
Week 4: Canaries, dry-run simulation, and incident-runner integration
Week 5: Docs, training runbook for SRE, and handoff to support team

Implement minimal sandbox runtime and CLI (eng: Arjun, Noor)

telemetry_checks: Execution latency per tasklet < 3s median for quick ops flows
Dry-run match rate (predicted vs actual) >= 80% for core set
Audit log size per execution < 10KB after redaction for 95% of runs
rollout_plan: Start with a 2-person SRE alpha in a staging account (week 3), expand to 5 beta teams in a Reserved sandbox (week 4), then enable read-only gallery for all engineers and opt-in execute for support during week 5. Monitor failure rate and pause rollout if failure spikes > 5% above baseline.
qa_notes: Create synthetic incident harness to run tasklets against staging clusters
Validate rollback paths by injecting failure after step N and asserting system returns to previous known good state
Pen-test sandbox escape attempts before enabling cross-namespace scope
